ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r5.claim: The Prophet’s duty is to warn of the Hereafter and communicate Islam, not to ensure that people become Muslims or to overburden himself over their refusal.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r5.anchor: the real responsibility of the Prophet (sws) is to warn people of the Hereafter

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.claim: Luxury and self-sufficiency signal rejection and readiness for disbelief and wrongdoing; affliction can purify, humble, and soften hearts, so the more deeply tried are more receptive to fear.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.anchor: الاستغناء والترف أمارة الإعراض وعدم القابلية والتهيؤ للكفر والفجور ، وإلى أن المصائب أمارة للطهارة والإقبال واستكانة القلوب

ELMALILI:80:3-42/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r6.claim: The Prophet bears no responsibility if the self-sufficient person refuses purification or Islam, but ignoring a Muslim who seeks instruction entails responsibility; guidance efforts toward unbelievers remain permissible in principle.
ELMALILI:80:3-42/r6.anchor: müstağnînin temizlenmemesinden, İslâm’a girmemesinden sana bir mes’ûliyet teveccüh etmez

SAMIN-DURR:80:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:7/r1.claim: ألا يزكى is the subject, and عليك is its predicate: the man’s failure to purify himself is not your responsibility.
SAMIN-DURR:80:7/r1.anchor: ألا يزكى }: مبتدأ خبره عليك، أي: ليس عليك عدم تزكيته.

ASAD-NOTES:80:3#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:3#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:3#n3/r1.claim: Asad's literal gloss says it is not upon the Prophet if the man does not attain purity.
ASAD-NOTES:80:3#n3/r1.anchor: Lit., "it is not upon thee (alayka) that he does not attain to purity".

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r9.claim: The phrase diminishes the unbeliever's importance and urges the Prophet to stop attending to him: it is no concern if he fails to prosper or purify himself of disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r9.anchor: وما عليك ألا يزكى: تحقير لأمر الكافر وحض على الإعراض عنه وترك الاهتمام به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p41/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p41/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p41/r1.claim: The Prophet bears no blame if the disbeliever does not purify himself; eagerness for his conversion should not cause the Prophet to turn away from someone who has believed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p41/r1.anchor: وليس عليك بأس في أن لا يزكى بالأسلام حتى يبعثك الحرص على إسلامه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p41/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p41/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p41/r2.claim: Ma is negative and the clause is circumstantial from the subject of taṣaddā; alternatively it is an interrogative repudiation meaning the same thing: what harm is it if he does not purify himself?
ALUSI-FULL:v30p41/r2.anchor: فما نافية والجملة حال من ضمير تصدى والممنوع عنه في الحقيقة الأعراض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r1.claim: A preceding citation of 6:52 praises God’s kindness to His servants and prays not to be cut off from His mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r1.anchor: [ الأنعام : 52 ] فتبارك ربنا ما أعظم لطفه بعبيده اللهم لا تؤيسنا من رحمتك ولا تقنطنا من لطفك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r2.claim: The Prophet bears no blame if the proud man fails to purify himself, even minimally; his duty is only to convey the message.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r2.anchor: بين له أنه سالم من ذلك فقال : { وما } أي فعلت ذلك والحال أنه ما { عليك }

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r3.claim: The wording may also be parsed as a question: what burden would fall on the Prophet if the man were not purified?
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استفهاما أي وأي شيء يكون عليك في عدم تزكيه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r4.claim: One should still strive to purify a follower when there is reason to expect that he will accept guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r4.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أنه يجب الاجتهاد في تزكية التابع الذي عرف منه القبول

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r9.claim: The passage uses ḥtibāk: mentioning the rich first implies the poor second, while the seeker’s coming and fear imply their opposites in the first case.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r9.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الغنى أولا يدل على الفقر ثانيا

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.claim: In another account, ʿAʾisha says the Prophet was addressing Quraysh leaders including Abu Jahl and ʿUtba when Ibn Umm Maktum came; the Prophet turned away, and the quoted passage was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مجلس من ناس من وجوه قريش منهم أبو جهل بن هشام وعتبة بن ربيعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r12.claim: The phrase means that it would not harm or concern the Prophet if the wealthy man failed to purify himself or prosper; it urges him not to concern himself with them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r12.anchor: وما عليك ألا يزكى وما يضرك ألا يفلح، فهذا حض على الإعراض عن أمرهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28/r1.claim: You bear no responsibility if the person you invite to Islam does not accept it; your duty is only to convey the message.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى وما عليك أي أي شيء عليك في أن لا يسلم من تدعوه إلى الإسلام يعني أنه ليس عليه إلا البلاغ

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.claim: They say it was revealed when Ibn Umm Maktūm interrupted the Prophet's effort to convert Meccan leaders; the Prophet turned back to them and God rebuked him.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم أتى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored him, welcomed him as the man over whom his Lord reproached him, and asked his needs.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.anchor: فكان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بعد ذلك يكرمه، وإذا رآه قال: مرحبا بمن عاتبني ربي فيه،

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.speaker: أنس
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya in armor with a black banner.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.anchor: قال أنس: رأيته يوم القادسية، عليه درع، ومعه راية سوداء.

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd relates the saying that if the Messenger concealed revelation, he would have concealed this passage.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان يقال: لو كتم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - شيئا من الوحي لكتم هذا.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#5/r1.claim: The Prophet is not responsible for making the man accept Islam and purify himself; his duty is only to deliver the message.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#5/r1.anchor: وليس عليك بأس فى أن يتزكى بالاسلام ان عليك إلا البلاغ

RAZI-FULL:v31p52#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#4/r1.claim: You are not responsible if the person you call does not accept Islam; your duty is only to convey, so zeal for their conversion must not turn you away from a believer.
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#4/r1.anchor: فإنه ليس عليك إلا البلاغ ، أي لا يبلغن بك الحرص على إسلامهم إلى أن تعرض عمن أسلم

SULAMI:v2p373#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#4/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p373#4/r1.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads the phrase as treating with contempt the one who turns away.
SULAMI:v2p373#4/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : استهانة بمن اعرض عنه

SULAMI:v2p373#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#4/r2.speaker: جعفر الخلدي
SULAMI:v2p373#4/r2.claim: Jaʿfar al-Khuldī says the Prophet was not honored by being directed toward someone God had not honored with guidance or shown gnosis.
SULAMI:v2p373#4/r2.anchor: قال جعفر الخلدي : لم يكرم بالإقبال على من لم يكرمه بالهداية ولم يريه بالمعرفة

TABRISI:80:20/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:80:20/r6.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, also named Abdullah ibn Shurayh ibn Malik ibn Rabiʿa al-Fihri, when he came as the Prophet was urging Quraysh leaders toward Islam.
TABRISI:80:20/r6.anchor: قيل نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وهو عبد الله بن شريح بن مالك ابن ربيعة الفهري

TABRISI:80:20/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:80:20/r7.claim: The Prophet was speaking with ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, Abu Jahl, al-ʿAbbas, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf when Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked to be taught; the Prophet turned away, thinking the leaders might scorn a following of blind people and slaves.
TABRISI:80:20/r7.anchor: وذلك أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام والعباس بن عبد المطلب وأبيا وأمية ابني خلف

TABRISI:80:20/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:80:20/r8.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktum, greeted him as the man for whom his Lord had reproached him, asked about his needs, and appointed him deputy in Medina twice.
TABRISI:80:20/r8.anchor: وكان رسول الله بعد ذلك يكرمه

TABRISI:80:20/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABRISI:80:20/r9.claim: Anas ibn Malik says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at al-Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black standard.
TABRISI:80:20/r9.anchor: وقال أنس بن مالك: فرأيته يوم القادسية وعليه درع ومعه راية سوداء

TABRISI:80:20/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r10.speaker: المرتضى علم الهدى
TABRISI:80:20/r10.claim: Al-Murtada rejects identifying the passage's subject as the Prophet: the text does not name him, and frowning at a believing seeker or preferring rich people to the poor conflicts with his noble character.
TABRISI:80:20/r10.anchor: قال المرتضى علم الهدى قدس الله روحه: ليس في ظاهر الآية دلالة

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.claim: The proposed honorific reading of the switch from third to second person does not fit the direct address that follows, whose rebuke is stronger and has no conciliatory intimacy.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يلائمه الخطاب في قوله بعد { أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى }

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.claim: The rebuked pattern is that the Prophet attends to wealthy people who scorn the truth, unconcerned whether they purify themselves, while neglecting the person earnestly seeking purification and fearing God.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.anchor: أنك تعتني وتقبل على من استغنى واستكبر عن اتباع الحق وما عليك أن لا يزكى وتتلهى وتعرض عمن يجتهد في التزكي وهو يخشى

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r6.claim: One reading takes mā as negative: it is no fault of yours if the rich man does not purify himself, so eagerness for his conversion should not divert you from one who already accepted Islam.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r6.anchor: قيل { ما } نافية والمعنى وليس عليك بأس أن لا يتزكى حتى يبعثك الحرص

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r7.claim: A second reading takes mā as an incredulous question: what obligation falls on you if he does not cleanse himself of disbelief and sin? You are only a messenger responsible for conveying.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r7.anchor: وقيل { ما } للاستفهام الإنكاري والمعنى وأي شيء يلزمك

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r8.claim: The most contextually apt reading is that the Prophet should not concern himself with the rich man's failure to purify himself; the interrogative reading comes next, and the negative reading is least apt.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r8.anchor: وقيل المعنى ولا تبالي بعدم تطهره من دنس الكفر والفجور وهذا المعنى أنسب لسياق العتاب ثم الذي قبله ثم الذي قبله

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r12.claim: The Prophet bears no responsibility if the wealthy man does not accept Islam and leave disbelief; his duty is only to convey.

BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r11.claim: The Prophet bears no blame or burden if the self-satisfied man does not become purified by Islam; there is no need to prioritize him over someone who has accepted guidance.
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r11.anchor: وليس عليك بأس ووزر ووبال في أن لا يتزكى ذلك المستغني بالإسلام

BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r12.claim: One should not press Islam upon a person with no receptivity who loves the present world and is blind to the hereafter; the verse also belittles the one who turns away.
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r12.anchor: وكيف تحرض على الإسلام من ليس له قابلية وقد خلق على حب الدنيا والعمى

BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r13.claim: Mā is negative; the implied preposition fī is linked to an omitted noun, and the clause is circumstantial to taṣaddā, reinforcing the rebuke.
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r13.anchor: فما نافية وكلمة في المقدرة متعلقة باسم ما وهو محذوف والجملة حال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r2.claim: The Prophet is not responsible if the man does not accept Islam; his duty is only to convey the message.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r2.anchor: { وما عليك ألا يزكى } أي شيء عليك في أن لا يسلم؛ لأنه ليس عليك إسلامه، إنما عليك البلاغ.

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r13.claim: The Prophet is not answerable if the other man is not purified; his duty is only to convey the message.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r13.anchor: فأنت لا تؤخذ بألا يتزكى هو فإنما عليك البلاغ

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.claim: The whole passage is a reproach directed to the Prophet on behalf of the poor.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.anchor: وهذا كله من قبيل العتاب معه لأجل الفقراء

ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r4.claim: The point is: what responsibility is yours if the person you invite to Islam does not accept it?
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r4.anchor: أي أي شيء عليك أن لا يسلم من تدعوه إلى الإسلام

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.claim: ʿAbasa pairs with al-Nāziʿāt and shares its central theme, discourse style, and reasoning; the changed sequence of topics gives this sūrah its distinct majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.anchor: There is no basic difference between the central theme of both sūrahs.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r8.claim: The phrase means that the person may not believe or be guided; the Prophet's duty is only to convey the message.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r8.anchor: لا يؤمن ولا يهتدي، إن عليك إلا البلاغ.

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r9.claim: The Prophet is not accountable if the man does not convert; eagerness for his Islam should not cause neglect of one who has accepted it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r9.anchor: وليس عليك بأس في أن لا يتزكى بالإسلام حتى يبعثك الحرص على إسلامه إلى الإعراض عمن أسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r10.claim: The point agrees with the statement that the Messenger's duty is only to convey the message.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects this opening to the prior calls to heed and fear: humble people whom the world overlooks are especially cared for and chosen by God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r1.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما قال سبحانه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r2.claim: The saying that a disheveled, dusty person whom people ignore could swear an oath that God would fulfill illustrates the hidden rank of the humble.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r2.anchor: إجابة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأعلى منزلته لديه ( رب أشعث أغبر لا يؤبه له لو أقسم على الله لأبره )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r3.claim: Ibn Umm Maktūm was the Prophet’s muezzin and the man whose visit occasioned the sūra’s admonition.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r3.anchor: ومنهم ابن مكتوب الأعمى مؤذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو الذي بسببه نزلت السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r4.claim: The rebuke teaches the Prophet to remain patiently with people like Ibn Maktūm and not to despise them, echoing other admonitions and the command not to drive away those who seek God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r4.anchor: وتنبيها على أن يعمل نفسه الكريمة على مصابرة أمثال ابن مكتوم وأن لا يحتقر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r5.claim: Ibn Maktūm sought instruction while the Prophet addressed a Quraysh notable whose conversion he hoped would save the man and his kin; attending to that hope led him to neglect the immediate visitor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r5.anchor: لما دخل عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم ابن أم مكتون سائلا ومسترشدا وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم يكلم رجلا من أشراف قريش

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r2.claim: The description of the Prophet as a warner to those who fear applies to Ibn Umm Maktūm.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r2.anchor: كابن أم مكتوم , من نمط ما نزل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r3.claim: The command to keep company with those who call upon God morning and evening is another passage revealed in the pattern of Ibn Umm Maktūm’s case.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r3.anchor: نمط ما نزل في ابن أم مكتوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r8.claim: Mā is negative; ʿalayka is the fronted predicate and allā yazakkā is the subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r8.anchor: و { ما } نافية و { عليك } خبر مقدم . والمبتدأ { ألا يزكى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r9.claim: The Prophet is not responsible for the man’s failure to purify himself and need not exert himself beyond what God requires; this is divine gentleness toward His Messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r9.anchor: والمعنى : عدم تزكيه ليس محمولا عليك ، أي لست مؤاخذا بعدم اهتدائه حتى تزيد من الحرص على ترغيبه في الإيمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r8.claim: Mā is negative; ʿalayka is the fronted predicate, and the clause “that he be purified” is the delayed subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r8.anchor: و { ما } نافية و { عليك } خبر مقدم . والمبتدأ { ألا يزكى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r9.claim: The man’s failure to be guided is not the Prophet’s responsibility; he is not accountable for it and need not press beyond what God charged him with. This reassures him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r9.anchor: عدم تزكيه ليس محمولا عليك ، أي لست مؤاخذا بعدم اهتدائه حتى تزيد من الحرص على ترغيبه في الإيمان ما لم يكلفك الله به .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.claim: The self-sufficient person is the rich man whom the Prophet approached in hope of guidance, though he was not accountable if the man failed to purify himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.anchor: أي: أما الغني فأنت تتعرض له لعله يهتدي،

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r13.claim: The Prophet bears no responsibility if the wealthy man does not accept Islam and purify himself from unbelief.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r13.anchor: أي شيء يلزمك إن لم يسلم، ولم يتطهر من الكفر؟!

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r14.claim: Alternatively, the question means ‘Would it grieve you if he did not accept Islam?’ His unbelief cannot harm the Prophet, whose duty is only to convey.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r14.anchor: وقيل: معناه أيشق عليك إن لم يسلم؟! فلا يضرك كفره فإنما عليك البلاغ.

MUQATIL:80:1-7/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r8.claim: The Prophet is not responsible if that man does not believe or mend what he corrupted; Muqatil applies this to the group of men.
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r8.anchor: وما عليك ألا يؤمن ولا يصلح ما قد أفسد، هؤلاء النفر

QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r8.claim: The unbeliever's failure to be guided or believe is not the Prophet's responsibility; he is responsible only for conveying the message.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r8.anchor: أي لا يهتدي هذا الكافر ولا يؤمن، إنما أنت رسول، ما عليك إلا البلاغ
